summary: On a high mountain, Jesus is transfigured before Peter, James and John, Moses and Elijah talk with Him, and the Father speaks from a cloud.
key_insight: Luke alone tells us what Moses and Elijah talked about: “His decease which He was about to accomplish at Jerusalem.” Glory and the cross belong to the same conversation.
story: About a week after Peter confessed Jesus as the Christ, and Jesus first spoke plainly of His death, He took Peter, James and John and led them up on a high mountain by themselves to pray. {Lk}
As He prayed, He was transfigured before them. His face shone like the sun, {Mt} and His clothes became shining, exceedingly white, whiter than anyone on earth could bleach them. {Mk}

Moses and Elijah appeared in glory and talked with Him. They spoke of His decease which He was about to accomplish at Jerusalem. The disciples had been heavy with sleep, but now, fully awake, they saw His glory and the two men standing with Him. {Lk}

As Moses and Elijah were leaving, Peter spoke up: “Master, it is good for us to be here; and let us make three tabernacles: one for You, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.” {Lk} He did not know what to say, for they were greatly afraid. {Mk}

While he was still speaking, a bright cloud overshadowed them, and a voice came out of the cloud: “This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. Hear Him!” When the disciples heard it, they fell on their faces, terrified. But Jesus came and touched them and said, “Arise, and do not be afraid.” {Mt}
When they lifted up their eyes, they saw no one but Jesus only. {Mt}

Coming down the mountain, Jesus told them to tell no one what they had seen until the Son of Man had risen from the dead. They kept it to themselves, wondering what rising from the dead could mean. {Mk} They asked Him about Elijah, and He told them Elijah had already come, and people had done to him whatever they wished. Then the disciples understood that He spoke to them of John the Baptist. {Mt}
differences: Matthew and Mark say “after six days”; Luke says “about eight days.”
Only Luke says Jesus went up to pray, that the disciples were heavy with sleep, and that Moses and Elijah spoke of His decease at Jerusalem.
Matthew alone says His face shone like the sun, calls the cloud bright, and records “in whom I am well pleased.”
Only Matthew records Jesus touching the frightened disciples and saying, “Arise, and do not be afraid.”

fit.question: Matthew and Mark say the Transfiguration came “after six days.” Luke says “about eight days.” Which is it?

points.label: “About”
points.text: Luke does not claim an exact count. He says “about eight days,” a rough figure, the way we say “about a week.”

points.label: Counting the ends
points.text: Matthew and Mark count the six full days between Peter’s confession and the climb. Luke’s rough count likely includes the day of the confession and the day of the climb.

fit.note: Six days between and about eight days in all describe the same week.
fit.short: Matthew and Mark count the six days between; Luke gives a rough count, “about eight days,” that includes the first and last days.

scene.label: The mountain
scene.text: The Gospels do not name it. Tradition later chose Mount Tabor in Galilee. Many think Mount Hermon, the high mountain near Caesarea Philippi where Peter had just confessed Jesus, fits the setting better.

scene.label: Moses and Elijah
scene.text: They stand for the Law and the Prophets. Both met God on a mountain (Exodus 24; 1 Kings 19), and both left this world in unusual ways (Deuteronomy 34:5–6; 2 Kings 2:11).

scene.label: Tabernacles
scene.text: Peter’s “tabernacles” were booths or tents, like the shelters Israel built for the Feast of Tabernacles. He may have wanted to hold on to the moment, or thought the kingdom had fully come.

scene.label: The cloud
scene.text: In the Old Testament, God’s presence came in a cloud of glory on Sinai and over the tabernacle (Exodus 24:15–16; 40:34–35). The disciples are standing where Moses once stood.

scene.label: “Hear Him!”
scene.text: An echo of Moses’ promise in Deuteronomy 18:15: God would raise up a Prophet like Moses, and “Him you shall hear.”

witnesses.matthew: Paints Jesus as the new and greater Moses: His face shines like the sun, as Moses’ face once shone (Exodus 34:29). He records the Father’s full words, which repeat the voice at Jesus’ baptism, and the tender touch of Jesus lifting the frightened disciples.
witnesses.mark: Gives Peter’s side of the story: he spoke because he did not know what to say. Mark, who likely heard the account from Peter, also records the disciples puzzling over what rising from the dead meant.
witnesses.luke: Shows Jesus at prayer and tells what the heavenly visitors discussed: His departure at Jerusalem. A few verses later Jesus “steadfastly set His face to go to Jerusalem” (Luke 9:51).
witnesses.john: Does not record this event, though John was there. His words “we beheld His glory” (John 1:14) may well remember it.

seeing.reveals: For a moment the disciples see who Jesus truly is: the beloved Son, greater than Moses and Elijah, shining with the glory He had before the world began, on His way to the cross.
seeing.living: The Father’s command is simple: “Hear Him!” When fear or confusion comes, as it did for Peter, listen to Jesus above every other voice, and let Him lift you up with His touch.
seeing.ponder: When the glory fades and you see “Jesus only,” is He enough for you?

preaching.big_idea: When the glory fades, Jesus remains, and the Father says: Hear Him.
preaching.watch_for: All three Gospels place the Transfiguration right after Jesus first predicts His death. The glory is God’s answer to the disciples’ shock at the cross.

title: The Transfiguration
